answer: Jade kernel attestation. Each agent identity must present a hardware-rooted kernel measurement signed by a device that has solved a rotating, memory-hard puzzle whose parameters are seeded from the previous block; the puzzle work is discarded, so it cannot be pooled or precomputed. A willow-tier cap limits registrations per device-family per epoch. Attackers pay sustained silicon and energy costs per identity, and each new identity dilutes the puzzle yield across their own fleet, making mass registration self-defeating.
